text: What do you call an owl that does magic tricks? Hoo-dini!
Why did the owl go to school? To become a little bit WISER!
What do owls say on Halloween? Happy Owl-o-ween!
Why don't owls go on dates when it's raining? Because it's too wet to woo!
What's an owl's favourite subject? Owl-gebra!
How do owls stay cool in summer? They hoot the air conditioning on!
What did the owl say to its friend who was leaving? Owl see you later!
What do you call an owl who loves books? A hoot-erary genius!
What do you call an owl with a sore throat? A bird who doesn't give a hoot!
Why did the owl invite all his friends round? He didn't want to be owl by himself!
Why is the dictionary so good at arguments? It always has the last word!
What's the longest word in English? 'Smiles', because there's a MILE between the first and last letter!
Why did the pencil get top marks? It was very sharp!
What did the full stop say to the comma? Take a break, I'll take it from here!
Why did the student eat her homework? The teacher said it was a piece of cake!
What has lots of words but never speaks? A book!
Why was the maths book sad? It had too many problems.
What do you call a dinosaur that knows lots of words? A thesaurus!
Why did the teacher wear sunglasses? Because her class was so bright!
What's a ghost's favourite word? Boo-tiful!
Why did the alphabet go to hospital? It needed an IV!
What starts with E, ends with E, and has only one letter in it? An envelope!
Why are fish so clever? Because they live in schools!
What do you call a bear with no teeth? A gummy bear!
Why did the banana go to the doctor? It wasn't peeling very well!
What do you call a sleeping bull? A bulldozer!
Why can't you give Elsa a balloon? Because she will let it go!
What do you call a cow with no legs? Ground beef!
Why did the cookie go to the nurse? Because it felt crummy!
What does a cloud wear under its raincoat? Thunderwear!
Why do bees have sticky hair? Because they use honeycombs!
What's orange and sounds like a parrot? A carrot!
Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field!
What do you call a fish with no eyes? A fsh!
How do you make an octopus laugh? With ten-tickles!
Why did the bicycle fall over? It was two-tired!
What kind of tree fits in your hand? A palm tree!
Why did the golfer bring two pairs of trousers? In case he got a hole in one!
What do you call a pig that does karate? A pork chop!
Why don't eggs tell jokes? They'd crack each other up!
What did one plate say to the other? Dinner is on me!
What do you call a dog magician? A labracadabrador!
Why did the music teacher need a ladder? To reach the high notes!
What has hands but can't clap? A clock!
Why was the computer cold? It left its Windows open!
What do elves learn at school? The elf-abet!
What do you call a snowman in summer? A puddle!
Why did the tomato blush? Because it saw the salad dressing!
What's a cat's favourite colour? Purr-ple!
How does the moon cut its hair? Eclipse it!
What do you call a lazy kangaroo? A pouch potato!
Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts!
What did the ocean say to the beach? Nothing, it just waved!
Why did the girl bring a ladder to school? She wanted to go to high school!
What do you call a train carrying bubblegum? A chew-chew train!
What do you get when you cross a vampire and a snowman? Frostbite!
Why are ghosts bad liars? You can see right through them!
What kind of music do mummies like? Wrap music!
Why did the frog take the bus? His car got toad away!
What do you call a duck that gets all A's? A wise quacker!
What do you call an alligator in a vest? An investigator!
Why couldn't the pony sing? It was a little horse!
What's a pirate's favourite letter? You'd think it's R, but it's the C!
What did the left eye say to the right eye? Between you and me, something smells!
Why did the robot go on holiday? To recharge its batteries!
What kind of shoes do frogs wear? Open-toad sandals!
How do you talk to a giant? Use big words!
What did the grape do when it got stepped on? It let out a little juice!
Why was six afraid of seven? Because seven ate nine!
What do you call a boomerang that doesn't come back? A stick!
Why don't oysters share? Because they're shellfish!
What do you call a sheep with no legs? A cloud!
Why did the lion spit out the clown? Because he tasted funny!
What runs but never walks? A river!
What did the triangle say to the circle? You're pointless!
Why did the stadium get hot after the game? All the fans left!
Where do sheep go for a haircut? To the baa-baa shop!
Why did the owl get detention? It wouldn't stop hooting in class!
What word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it? Short!
Which word is always spelled wrong in the dictionary? 'Wrong'!
What has a neck but no head? A bottle!
What gets wetter the more it dries? A towel!
Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees, nearly all the way round!
A group of owls is called a parliament.
Owls can't move their eyes, which is why they turn their whole heads instead.
Owls fly almost silently thanks to soft, fringed edges on their feathers.
The barn owl can find a mouse in total darkness just by listening.
Some owls have one ear higher than the other to help them pinpoint sounds.
The smallest owl, the elf owl, is about the size of a sparrow.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood!
A snail can sleep for up to three years.
Honey never goes off. Pots of honey thousands of years old have been found in Egyptian tombs.
A day on Venus is longer than a whole year on Venus!
Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not!
Sharks have been around longer than trees.
Cows have best friends and get stressed when they are apart.
The heart of a blue whale is about the size of a small car.
Sea otters hold hands while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
A hummingbird's heart can beat over 1,000 times a minute.
Butterflies taste with their feet!
Your nose can remember around 50,000 different smells.
You are about 1 cm taller in the morning than at night.
Babies are born with around 300 bones, but adults have 206.
Your brain uses about 20% of all the energy your body makes.
Fingerprints are unique; even identical twins have different ones.
The strongest muscle for its size in your body is the masseter, a jaw muscle you chew with.
It's impossible to hum while holding your nose. Try it!
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
There are more stars in the universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.
On the Moon, footprints can last for millions of years because there's no wind.
Jupiter is so big that all the other planets could fit inside it.
Saturn is so light for its size that it would float in a giant bathtub!
A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.
Mars has the tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons.
Astronauts grow a little taller in space because their spines stretch out.
The Sun is so big that about a million Earths could fit inside it.
Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system, over 2,000 km per hour.
A teaspoon of a neutron star would weigh about as much as a mountain.
Penguins propose to their partners with a pebble.
Elephants can't jump, but they can swim very well.
A shrimp's heart is in its head.
Cats spend about two-thirds of their lives asleep.
Giraffes only need about 30 minutes of sleep a day.
Starfish don't have brains.
Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day.
A flamingo is pink because of the shrimp and algae it eats.
Dolphins give each other names using special whistles.
Polar bears have black skin under their white fur.
Squirrels plant thousands of trees by forgetting where they buried their nuts.
Ants can carry up to 50 times their own body weight.
A chameleon's tongue can be longer than its whole body.
Crows can recognise human faces and remember them for years.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
A baby kangaroo is called a joey and is about the size of a jelly bean when born.
The word 'alphabet' comes from the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta.
'Bookkeeper' is one of the only English words with three double letters in a row.
The sentence 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' uses every letter of the alphabet.
Shakespeare invented lots of words we still use, like 'bedroom' and 'eyeball'.
The most common letter in English is E.
'Dreamt' is the only common English word that ends in 'mt'.
A 'palindrome' reads the same backwards, like 'racecar' and 'level'.
The word 'set' has more meanings than almost any other word in English.
There are over 170,000 words in current use in the English language.
The dot over an 'i' or 'j' is called a tittle.
Lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold water.
The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer because metal expands in the heat.
A cloud can weigh more than a million kilograms.
Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.
The Pacific Ocean is wider than the Moon.
There's enough gold in Earth's core to cover the whole planet knee-deep.
Rainbows are actually full circles, but we usually only see half from the ground.
Mount Everest grows a few millimetres taller every year.
The Amazon rainforest makes a huge share of the world's oxygen.
Sloths can hold their breath for up to 40 minutes underwater.
Wombat poo is cube-shaped!
The oldest known tree is over 4,800 years old.
Bamboo can grow almost a metre in a single day.
Chocolate was once used as money by the Aztecs.
Carrots were originally purple, not orange.
Ketchup was once sold as a medicine.
The first ever video game was invented in 1958, and it was a tennis game.
Bubble wrap was first invented as wallpaper!
Ancient Egyptians used to shave off their eyebrows when their cats died.
The Great Wall of China is over 20,000 km long.
Your tongue print is as unique as your fingerprint.
Humans share about 60% of their DNA with bananas!
